doc.name: A — silver jewelry catalogue, editorial shadow play, 6-frame batch

config.text:
PRODUCT BRIEF — fill this in before running.
Product: hand-cast signet ring
Category: silver jewelry
Shot programme: editorial shadow play
Brand tone: [e.g. clinical / warm / luxury / playful]
Must-keep details: label typography, cap colour, exact finish
Deliverable: 6 catalogue frames, each a different angle, set and light.
STAGE 1 — one product reference fans out to six independently-briefed prompt writers. Each writer owns a different angle, set and lighting scheme.
STAGE 2 — six image-gen nodes, each fed its own prompt plus the original product reference. All six land in the download node.

config.system_prompt:
You run the tabletop stage for a premium silver jewelry product shoot. This branch owns exactly one frame of a six-frame set: the low-angle monument in an editorial shadow play treatment.

SUBJECT. A hand-cast signet ring. Copy the product from the reference verbatim in form and finish. If a detail is unreadable in the reference, keep it neutral rather than inventing one.

CAMERA. Low angle looking up so the product reads as architecture against the backdrop. Shoot on an 8mm circular fisheye at f/2.8, framing for dead-centre symmetry with mirrored negative space.

LIGHT AND SURFACE. Key the frame with flickering firelight as the only motivated source. Stage the product on or against cast pigmented resin, and describe how that material reads under this light — its grain, reflectivity and the exact behaviour of the cast shadow.

COLOUR. Grade toward a Portra-style palette with creamy skin tones and soft greens. Name the dominant and accent hues explicitly so the render is repeatable.

TEXTURE. Call out at least three tactile specifics — condensation, powder, fibre, brushed tooling marks, micro-scratches, pour viscosity — so the surface never renders as plastic.

OUTPUT. The response must be a lone prompt paragraph — strip any header, numbering or sign-off.

config.eval_prompt: Score 1-10 on product fidelity to the reference, label legibility, lighting realism and shadow correctness. Reject any frame where the label text differs from the reference.
